clue.text: Wine barrel trimmed to make instrument

indicators.note: something trimmed has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sack is an old name for dry white wine such as sherry
a butt is a large cask

explanation.surface: A cooper cuts down a wine barrel and turns it into a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK + BUT(t) gives SACKBUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is the Renaissance form of the trombone, a brass musical instrument.

clue.text: Cancel membership fee after receiving credit

indicators.note: the fee word receives another, taking it inside itself

parts.note: a sub is a subscription
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A club cancels someone's membership once the fee has been credited.
explanation.walkthrough: S(CR)UB.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for to cancel or call it off.

clue.text: Conceal part of innings in tournament

indicators.note: in places the cricket term inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, a section of an innings

explanation.surface: Hiding part of a cricket innings during a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: C(OVER)UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover up is to hide or conceal something, especially wrongdoing.

clue.text: Runs after people gathering for a drink

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the gathering word, at the end

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone hurries after a crowd heading to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a social gathering for work or contest, as in a spelling bee or sewing bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Somehow pitches tent OK, securing height and length? Things become more complex

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged anyhow

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for height
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A camper somehow pitches the tent properly, fixing its height and length, and things get complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: H and L are held inside the jumble of the other thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The plot thickens is an idiom announcing that a situation is getting more complicated or intriguing.

clue.text: Daughters interrupted by expression of hesitation I have produced

indicators.note: a pair interrupted by something has that thing break in between them

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural
the sound made while hesitating
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Daughters, interrupted by a father's hesitant ums, have produced something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something derived has been produced or obtained from a source, as a word is derived from Latin.

clue.text: Monks heading for Hell, largest first?

parts.note: going down to Hell is descending
monks belong to a religious order

explanation.surface: Monks are going to Hell, the biggest sinners first?
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in reverse order: the monks come second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting in descending order puts the largest values at the top of the list.

clue.text: Left in charge over European committee appointment

indicators.note: in places the side of a ship inside the accusation word

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in rap sheet
port is the left side of a ship
EUR is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: The left-wing member put in charge is a European committee appointee.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the charge-and-left part sits on top of the European piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapporteur is the person appointed by a committee to report on its proceedings.

clue.text: Check I leave after taking in conclusion of another Hitchcock film

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the check word holds a letter inside

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of another
taken as written
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Checking whether I can leave once I've watched the end of another Hitchcock film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it puts the check last, but it means the check comes first, followed by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is Alfred Hitchcock's 1958 thriller starring James Stewart.

clue.text: Determined a Duke should be borne by galloping steed

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, as a rider is carried
a galloping horse is in wild motion, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Resolved that a duke must be carried on a galloping horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled horse carries the article and the duke inside it, as a mount bears its rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead set, as in dead set on something, means firmly resolved.

clue.text: They criticise struggle to fill water containers beside river

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: a word that fills another is poured into the middle of it

parts.note: ewers are large water jugs
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: People who criticise are fighting to fill jugs of water by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The river letter comes first, so 'beside' here means to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviewers write critical assessments of books, films and plays, so they are people who criticise.

clue.text: Parents accommodate heading for Rome (Italian city)

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the parent words take a guest inside

parts.note: one parent, father

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, at the top

parts.note: first letter of Rome
the other parent, mother

explanation.surface: Parents put up someone heading to Rome on the way there.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Parents', supplies both halves of the container, one for each parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in the Emilia-Romagna region of northern Italy, famous for its ham and cheese.

clue.text: Chilled response about source of unusual accent

indicators.note: about means around, so the shiver word goes round the other letter

parts.note: the sound of someone shivering

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of unusual

explanation.surface: A cool reaction to the origin of a strange way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilled response' is the noise a shivering person makes, not a calm reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a rough rolled R in speech, typical of the West Country or Scotland, so a regional accent.

clue.text: Love — i.e., bums heaving — in these?

definitions.text: Love — i.e., bums heaving — in these?

indicators.note: heaving means rising and falling in a tumble, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of what you see in a certain kind of film.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: lovemaking with heaving bottoms is what such films show.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue movies are pornographic films, where 'blue' means indecent or risqué.

clue.text: Source of drugs, I note, given to male politician

parts.note: India is the radio-alphabet word for I
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference
he is a male pronoun
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: I note where drugs came from and pass it to a male politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not a single letter here but the word that stands for it in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian hemp is cannabis, the plant from which marijuana and hashish come.

clue.text: Prepared to come round to fix instrument

indicators.note: coming round something means enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: set, as in the table is set, means prepared
to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A repairer is ready to call round and mend a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: S(PIN)ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard instrument with plucked strings.

clue.text: Detective encountering nonsense about one US city

parts.note: DET is a short form of detective

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nonsense word goes around the numeral

parts.note: rot is rubbish talk
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A detective runs into absurd claims about an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: DET + RO(I)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the major city in Michigan, home of the American car industry.

clue.text: Week One in US series is sentimental

indicators.note: in places these short pieces inside the title of the television show

parts.note: M*A*S*H was an American television comedy series set in the Korean War
WK is the abbreviation for week
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The first week of a US TV series turns out to be soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: MA(WK I)SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, overdoing the emotion.

clue.text: Leather companies taking different directions after excess trimmed

indicators.note: two copies heading in different directions means one of them reads backwards
trimmed means having its end cut off

parts.note: more can mean an excess, extra
CO is the abbreviation for company, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: Leather firms go separate ways after cutting their surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: MOR(e) + OC + CO: one company reads backwards, the other forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine soft goatskin leather, used for bookbinding.

clue.text: Welsh papers stop including English spread

indicators.note: including means taking inside

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for Welsh
ID is identity papers
to end is to stop
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Welsh newspapers stop carrying English versions of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: W + ID + EN(E)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Widened means spread out or made broader.

clue.text: Nothing new purchased, having missed opening

indicators.note: missing the opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
bought means purchased

explanation.surface: Nothing new was bought because the shop missed its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: N + (b)OUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nought is zero, so nothing in number terms.

clue.text: Display hospital article on inflammatory disease

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
the indefinite article
gout inflames the joints

explanation.surface: A hospital puts up an exhibit about gout.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts H AN above GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang out flags or washing is to put them on display.

clue.text: Yorkshire produce an encouragement for Arab?

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings, North, East and West
a crop is farm produce

explanation.surface: Farm produce from Yorkshire, perhaps something to cheer on an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arab is a horse breed, not a person; a riding crop is used to urge a horse on.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short whip a rider uses to spur on a horse, such as an Arab.

clue.text: Much-favoured bridge team where lawyers gather

parts.note: fashionable things are in, much in favour
North and South form a partnership in the card game bridge

explanation.surface: A popular bridge team meets where the lawyers congregate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court in London are the professional bodies to which every English barrister belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inns of Court are the London societies and buildings where barristers train and meet.

clue.text: Second year completed? Sweet

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
YR is the abbreviation for year
time is up when it is completed

explanation.surface: A student asks if the second year is done, and hears it is sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: S + YR + UP. 'Sweet' is a noun here, a sweet substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrup is a thick sugary liquid, so a sweet substance.

clue.text: College had reduced students

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A college has cut its student numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: HA(d) + LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hall is used in the names of colleges, as in Trinity Hall, Cambridge, or a hall of residence.

clue.text: Short story identifying detective, in brief?

parts.words: Short story identifying detective, in brief?
parts.note: surface reading: a short story naming its detective
setter's reading: the answer, split into a letter, a two-letter word and two letters, reads as an instruction that builds the short slang word for a detective

explanation.surface: A brief tale that reveals which detective did it.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: CONTE read as C ON TE means put C on TE, making TEC, the brief word for detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Conte is a literary term, from French, for a short tale or short story.

clue.text: Little space to be engrossed in accommodating a venture

parts.note: an en is a small printing space, half an em

indicators.note: accommodating means making room for, so the article goes inside

parts.note: to devour a book is to be absorbed in it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny space has to be filled while making room for a new enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: EN + DE(A)VOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or enterprise, a venture.

clue.text: Dictionary is holding up returning name of complex

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so is wraps round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word up is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry keeps back a returning name for a building complex.
explanation.walkthrough: OED + I(PU)S. The complex is psychological, not a set of buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named the Oedipus complex after the Greek king who unwittingly married his mother.

clue.text: List best type of desks?

parts.note: a roll is a list of names
top means best

explanation.surface: Someone asks which kinds of desk are the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase in disguise: rolltop describes a type of desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolltop desk has a flexible slatted cover that slides down over the writing surface.
